A late-night customer wants something small.

He wanted a bottle of water but wouldn't come through the door. I held it up from behind the counter. This one? He nodded. I took it outside and he counted coins into my hand, very slowly, looking over my shoulder. There was nobody in the shop. I checked anyway. He asked if the lights were always that bright. I said yes. He said I used to work here. The bottle slipped out of his hand and rolled under a parked car before he'd opened it. Neither of us moved to get it. I could see his feet properly now. One shoe was tied and the other had no lace. I asked if he needed me to phone someone. He shook his head so hard I stopped asking.
First train home
Travel while everyone else is waking up.

People were getting on with coffees and clean hair. I had fryer smell in my sleeves. A woman sat next to me, then got up again when another seat came free. Fair enough. I closed my eyes and counted stations by the bends. Missed mine anyway. At the next one I got off, crossed the bridge, waited on the other side. The same woman was there. She'd missed hers too. We didn't speak but I felt slightly better about the whole morning.
Radio off
An ordinary sound keeps you company.

Turned the radio off because the same advert had played four times. Without it I could hear someone coughing in the stockroom. Went to look. Nobody. Turned the radio back on and stayed near the front until six.
Handover notes
Leave a note for the next shift.

Freezer two is leaking again.
Man in blue jacket has paid for the petrol, don't charge him twice.
Please stop putting the mop here.
I wrote those three things and sat looking at the page. I wanted to add that I'd heard someone crying in the toilets for nearly an hour and hadn't knocked. I had knocked once, lightly, but not enough that they had to answer. When they left they bought gum and said thank you. For the gum probably. I didn't write any of that. There wasn't really anything for the next shift to do about it. The mop had fallen over again so I picked it up.
Still here
Someone is late to relieve you.

At six I called. At six fifteen I called again. At half six I stopped being worried and started being angry. Then worried again. There isn't much else to this one. He arrived at seven with no excuse and I went home.
Aisle four
Find something left behind.

A little shoe behind the cleaning products. No child anywhere. I put it by the till and forgot about it until a man came in carrying the matching shoe. He asked where I'd found it. I showed him. He didn't pick it up.
Window above the bakery
A light in a window keeps you company.

The bakery upstairs light came on at four. I imagined a kettle, a cat, somebody sleeping badly. Once I went over after my shift and bought coffee. PRIVATE on the stairs at the back. Looked too long. Baker asked if I needed the toilet. Said no and left. I hadn't meant to be nosy but it felt different standing there than watching the window from across the road. Next morning I tried not to look. Looked anyway. Light was on.
Call me when you're awake
A conversation happens at the wrong time of day.

My sister called at two in the afternoon and asked why I sounded drunk. I said I'd been asleep. She said must be nice. I nearly put the phone down. Then she said Dad had fallen and I sat up too fast. She'd been trying since ten. My phone was under the pillow on silent. I asked which hospital and couldn't find a pen, wrote it with a finger on the blanket like that would help. She repeated it three times. I could hear traffic behind her. I asked if she was alright. She said she was looking for the car park ticket. I couldn't tell if she was crying or just out of breath.
Counting cans
A repetitive task becomes difficult.

Twelve in a case. Six cases on a shelf. Four shelves. I kept getting a different number because I'd start counting individual cans halfway through. There was one open case and that ruined everything. I took it off the shelf. Now there were five cases and a gap and I couldn't remember if I'd counted the gap. I know multiplication. I passed maths. At four in the morning it had become a trick someone was playing on me. I wrote the number from last week and put a question mark beside it. Then crossed out the question mark because it looked worse. The supervisor would probably count them again anyway. I sat on the floor for a minute before doing the bottles.
Sunday sleeping
Rest when the rest of the world is busy.

I got home at seven and the neighbour was already washing his car. The hose was across our gate. I stepped over it, caught my heel, nearly went over with my bag. He said morning in a cheerful voice and I said something back that might have been morning. Inside, the flat was too warm. I opened a window then shut it because he had started the pressure washer. Shower, toast, couldn't eat the toast. There was a message from my mother asking if I was coming for lunch. I typed that I'd try. I knew I wouldn't. I lay down with one leg outside the duvet because I couldn't decide if I was hot or cold. The pressure washer stopped and a dog started. Then the dog stopped and somebody began drilling. I laughed into the pillow, one dry breath, not because anything was funny. At eleven I woke up convinced I was late for work. Put one sock on before remembering it was my night off. The toast was still on the plate by the bed with a bite missing. I ate the cold corner while standing there in one sock and read Mum's reply. She'd put a portion aside. I didn't know how to say I was too tired to go and too hungry not to.
Five seconds ahead
You can see five seconds into the future.

Five seconds sounds useful until you try crossing a road. I saw myself get hit, stopped, then saw myself standing there not getting hit, so started, then saw the car again. I spent forty minutes at that crossing. Eventually a child took my hand because she thought I was frightened. I was frightened. She pulled me across and for five seconds I saw her grown up, which wasn't how it was supposed to work at all. I let go halfway. Car horn, shouting, her mother grabbing both of us by the coats. I tried to explain about the child but the mother thought I was making excuses. Then I saw her face five seconds ahead and it was mine. I hadn't figured out the rules properly. Maybe that was the problem with having a power nobody had tested.
Portal behind the cooker
A portal opens in your kitchen.

The portal was only wide enough for a plate. We sent a plate through. It came back washed. Sent another, same result. For six weeks this was excellent. Then a bill came through. The currency was teeth. We stopped sending plates. Whoever was on the other side started knocking.
Mute button
You discover a button that silences the world.

Pressed mute and everything stopped making noise except my knees. That was disappointing. Pressed again and the noise came back too loud. Held it down to reset and now I can hear whatever the trees are saying but not the kettle.
Sleep exchange
Trade something intangible.

You could sell an hour of sleep for enough to buy breakfast. Most people sold two. I sold four because rent was due and I thought coffee would cover the difference. It did for a week. Then I started seeing the buyers' dreams while I was awake. A woman in a yellow room arguing with a dog. A man whose hands were all thumbs. Nothing useful. I went back to the exchange and asked whether this was normal. The clerk said I'd ticked the shared experience box. I said I hadn't read it. She said nobody did. I wanted the hours back but she'd already bundled them with other people's and sold them as a package. Somewhere a rich man was sleeping through my childhood and I was trying to stay awake on a plastic chair under a light that buzzed in time with my teeth.
Application to be a planet
Fill in an impossible form.

The moon applied to be a planet. It had the size wrong and no references except Earth, who refused to sign because they weren't speaking. I don't know why planets would have forms. This was fun for about ten seconds and now it's just an office joke with planets in it.
Dog translation trial
An invention translates your pet's thoughts.

Translator said SAUSAGE when the dog wanted water. Broken probably. Then STEVE IS IN THE WALL. Steve was our dead dog, buried outside. We switched it off. Heard scratching behind the wardrobe later. Mouse. Caught it, put translator beside the box. WRONG HOUSE WRONG HOUSE until the speaker distorted. Took it outside and pointed towards next door. Didn't ask more. Maybe all animals think in capitals. I should have tested that before taking the wall bit seriously.
Tomorrow's roads
A map shows tomorrow instead of today.

The map showed a road through our house. Not near it, through the kitchen. I checked the date. Tomorrow. I rang the council and asked about planned works. They said no. I asked about unplanned works and the woman went quiet like I'd made a threat. By evening the kitchen tiles had turned black at one edge. I put a mug on the dark bit and it rolled towards the fridge, which had begun to lean. We moved everything into the hall except the cooker, too heavy. At midnight there was a white line running under the table. I stood on it in my socks and could feel warmth coming up from below. My partner said we should leave. I said I wanted to see where the road went. She said that was the stupidest thing I'd said all year and went without me.
Rewind
A small part of the day repeats.

I dropped the spoon. Picked it up. Dropped it. Picked it up. By the seventh time I was angry enough to kick it under the fridge. Now I was on my knees reaching for a spoon forever. An improvement technically.
Last message sent
A message arrives after its sender is gone.

Don't open the second one.
That was the first message. The second was an image, still downloading. I turned off wifi but the mobile data carried on. Turned that off too. The thumbnail stayed grey. The sender was my old number, from before I lost the phone in the river. I tried calling it. My phone rang in my hand while I was already making the call. That's impossible but I could see both screens, the outgoing call underneath and the incoming one on top. I pressed answer. No voice. Just water very close to the microphone and somebody breathing through their nose. The image finished downloading even though everything was off. I put the phone face down before it appeared. Then spent the next ten minutes wanting to look.
Minor archive
A machine remembers an unimportant detail.

The machine remembered the exact number of steps between my old bed and the bathroom. Eleven if the cupboard was shut. Thirteen if I went round it. I asked why it had kept that and deleted my university password. It said relevance was calculated differently now. Differently to what? No answer. I asked it to delete the steps. It asked if I was sure. Yes. It asked again. I got annoyed and confirmed with the password I could remember. That night I walked into the cupboard door in the dark. Different house, different cupboard. Same distance. I'm not sure whether this is a story about memory or just me not switching a light on.
Arrival window
Visitors arrive from somewhere unexpected.

They arrived folded. Like letters, except the folds kept changing until there was enough space for them to stand. We had built a landing pad and all the cameras were pointed at it, but they came through the space between two teeth in the mayor's mouth. He was in the middle of the welcome speech. There was a little crack, he spat something silver into his hand and it unfolded into three people and a table. Nobody clapped. The visitors put the table down and waited. We waited. After a while one of them pointed to the mayor's mouth and held up two fingers. Two more coming, apparently. He refused. Can't blame him. We offered other mouths, a dog, a mannequin from the clothes shop. They seemed offended by the mannequin, or frightened, hard to tell because their faces were moving in the wrong directions. The smallest visitor climbed onto the table and unfolded again, taller this time, with a hole through the middle. Through the hole we could see another table and somebody setting plates out. They weren't invading. Maybe they were late for dinner and our world was a corridor. I stepped closer to see what was on the plates. The visitor put a hand on my chest and pushed, gently but with no possibility of arguing, and I went back three steps without moving my feet.
dont send
Write a message you keep changing in your head.

typed are you coming then haha so it looked less angry. worse. dinner's nearly ready? too domestic. only four dates, one was accidentally at a party. made pasta for six because i didnt trust the packet. now stuck together in the sink. typing dots appeared then went away. put phone in cupboard. took it out becuase what if i couldnt hear. he sent a bent bike wheel. i said oh no are you okay then felt pleased which is horrible. he had a reason. i was reheating pasta already before he'd answered whether he could still get here. should have asked about his leg first.
Borrowed jumper
Borrow something and forget to return it.

it was his jumper but it didnt smell like him anymore because i'd washed it about ten times. he asked for it back and i said of course then couldnt find it. looked everywhere. it was on me. i was wearing it while looking for it. i don't think this needs to mean anything i'm just very tired.
start somewhere
Begin before you know what happens.
a woman gets off a bus carrying a fish in her hands. no bag just a fish. alive? i think alive. she has to keep going somewhere before it dies but why didnt she bring a bucket. stuck already.
you can't just turn up
An unexpected visit.

she knocked like she still lived here, three quick ones and then the handle. i'd changed the lock so the handle did nothing. she said oh through the door. i stood on the other side holding a sock because i'd been sorting laundry and suddnely couldnt put it down. she said can we talk. i said we are talking. that sounded clever in my head and stupid out loud. she put something through the letterbox. her old key. it hit my bare foot and i jumped and she thought i'd opened the door because the floor creaked. she started saying thank you before anything had happened. i wanted to open it then just to stop that sentence being wrong. instead i said give me a minute and walked into the kitchen with the sock. no idea what i needed a minute for.
Mum's phone
Explain a simple device to someone.

i said swipe up and she swiped sideways. up mum. she said i am. i took the phone and did it too fast and opened about twelve things at once. she watched me close them one by one. i hate how impatient i get about this. she taught me how to hold a spoon and i'm getting annoyed because she can't find a tiny picture of a gear. then she asked how to delete a message without the other person seeing and i stopped explaining. i said depends which app. she said never mind. i said show me. she held the phone against her chest like a book she didnt want me reading. i had no right to take it but i nearly did anyway.
Wrong name
Accidentally use an old name.

called him dan. he's david. in my defence both d but he wasn't interested. halfway upstairs with a mattress so he couldn't leave, could stop lifting though. did. mattress slowly folding over me while he asked who dan was. i said old friend. why didnt i just say cousin. dan is my cousin. now i'm explaining family through a mattress while the neighbour tries to squeeze past and david keeps saying he can't hear me.
Laundry again
A household task becomes a reminder.

one red sock in all the white stuff. not even mine. now everything's pink and i can't be bothered to be angry. wore the pink tshirt to work and somebody said it suited me. maybe the sock knows something.
not shouting
Try to speak calmly while upset.

i'm not shouting.
you are a bit.
i'm trying not to.
okay.
that was the whole problem, the okay. he said okay like he was putting a lid on something. i had rehearsed this on the bus and in the version on the bus he listened and i made sense. here i kept saying the same bit about the keys and he kept saying he'd already apologised. he had. i didnt know what i wanted after the apology. maybe for him to look as upset as i felt. i said forget it and he actually turned back to the television which made me want to say all of it again louder. instead i went into the hall and picked my keys up off the floor where i'd thrown them. very mature evening all round.
Saturday list
Make a list that becomes something else.

washing
milk
call mum
find the receipt
stop thinking about what she said
washing again because i forgot to start it
why would she say that in front of everyone though
milk, actually go and get the milk
I dont have a story today. just this list. going to leave it here because finishing something probably counts even if it's only a list i haven't done any of.
Photo booth
Try to take a photograph together.

first picture i sneezed. second picture she laughed at me sneezing. third picture we were both ready but the flash didnt go. fourth picture there wasnt supposed to be a fourth picture. we looked at each other and it flashed again. the machine started pritning and kept printing, a long strip winding onto the floor. us getting older, not dramatic old just different hair, her wearing glasses, me with a mark on my cheek. in one we werent looking at each other. i stepped out and the printing stopped. she stayed sitting there looking at the strip and i couldnt tell if she wanted to see more. i said probably some filter thing. she said yeah. neither of us picked it up. i went back for it later but the booth was being used by two kids in school uniforms and i didnt want to ask.
After the call
An ordinary action after important news.

i put the kettle on and forgot to put water in. it clicked off straight away. filled it. put it on again. there was a spoon in my hand and i don't remember getting it. that's all i can get down at the moment.
Three cups
Prepare for a visitor you are nervous about.

i put three cups out because i didn't know if he was bringing her. then two because why would he bring her. then three again because having the cup already there might make me look like the sort of person who was fine with it. i wasn't fine with anything that morning. the flat was too clean in the wrong places, i'd cleaned the skirting boards but there was a pile of underwear on the chair. i shoved it in the oven. dont ask. cupboard was full. i forgot about it until i decided to warm the pastries and then there was this horrible hot elastic smell and i had to open every window. so when he arrived i was standing in a coat in my own kitchen holding a tray of warm pants. he was alone. he looked at the tray then at me and for a second we were both trying so hard not to laugh that i thought maybe things could just go back. then he said he'd only come for the documents. i said i know. i did know. i put the tray down very carefully on the hob and went to get the envelope from the hall. it wasn't where i'd left it. i'd moved everything everything when i was cleaning and now i had to ask him to wait while i looked, which was the exact thing i had been trying not to ask.
